evidence.label: A high-arity counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow

headline: A tautological relation in genus 10^60 that Pixton’s original relations miss, in Chow and in cohomology.
scope: One explicit class on the space of stable curves of genus 10^60 with about 5 × 10^179 marked points.
plain: The space of stable curves carries natural classes, and mathematicians want every relation among them. Pixton proposed a system of relations and conjectured that it gives all of them. This paper claims to build a class that is zero in the Chow ring, and so in rational cohomology. It also claims that this class does not come from Pixton’s original system. The example has genus 10^60, far from any small case.
doesNot: This does not show that Pixton’s system fails in small genus, or give a corrected complete list.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: A. Pixton, who proposed the relation system and conjectured completeness
scorecard.significanceWhy: If correct, it disproves the Chow and cohomological forms of a central conjecture about relations on moduli of curves.

explanation:
Suppose you know three facts about some numbers a, b and c. You know a − b = 0 and b − c = 0. From those two rules you can derive a − c = 0. A list of rules is complete when every true relation can be derived this way. Proving rules is one problem. Knowing that the list is complete is a different and harder one.

Algebraic geometers face this problem for curves. A moduli space is a space whose points are themselves shapes. Here each point is a stable curve. That is a curve of some genus g, maybe with simple pinches called nodes, and n marked points. This space, written M̄_{g,n}, has a family of natural classes. These are building blocks for its Chow ring, a way of doing algebra with subspaces and how they intersect. The natural classes form the tautological ring. Describing every relation among them is a central problem in this area[1].

Pixton proposed a uniform system of relations in 2012 and conjectured that it is complete[2,3]. The relations themselves were later shown to hold. Pandharipande, Pixton and Zvonkine proved them in cohomology. Janda proved them in Chow[4]. Those results establish the relations. Completeness asks whether any further relations exist[5].

This paper claims a negative answer. It builds an explicit formal class Y outside Pixton’s original span[6]. Yet the image of Y in the rational Chow ring is zero[6]. So Y is a true relation that Pixton’s list does not produce. Applying the cycle-class map then gives the same failure in rational cohomology[7]. Cohomology is a coarser way of measuring a space, so a relation that holds in Chow also holds there.

The example is enormous. The genus is g = 10^60. The construction uses g colours and one factor for each set of three colours[8]. The number of such triples is D = g(g − 1)(g − 2)/6. That is about 1.67 × 10^179. The number of marked points is n = 3D, about 5.0 × 10^179[6]. To see the pattern at small size, take 5 colours. Then there would be 10 triples and 30 marked points. The paper does not claim the result for such small numbers. The large sizes leave room in the estimates and are not proposed as minimal[9].

The difficulty is that two separate claims are needed about the same class. One is that Y is not in Pixton’s span. The other is that Y is still zero in Chow. The paper claims to prove them with two different algebras[10]. A formal algebra can carry independent cubic coefficients and still kill everything in Pixton’s span. That shows Y lies outside the span[10]. The actual Chow correspondences of a curve satisfy an extra identity that forces Y to vanish[10]. That identity comes from a Quot scheme, a space that parametrizes quotients of a fixed sheaf on a surface.

Completeness is not the same as the Gorenstein property, which concerns pairings between classes of complementary degree[11]. Pixton showed that a related ring in genus 25 is not Gorenstein, while still proving completeness there[12]. Canning, Larson and Schmitt found a similar split on some compact-type spaces. This paper’s relation instead lives on the full space of stable curves[13]. It concerns Pixton’s original system, fixed precisely in the paper. The comparison throughout is with that explicit span[14].

How sure is this? No Lean formalization is listed for this paper in the openai/math release. So no computer proof checker has checked it. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: Major only if the proof holds. No Lean formalization is listed and no specialist review is published. The example is astronomically large and says nothing about small genus.

glossary.meaning: A space whose points are themselves shapes, here curves with marked points.
A curve that may have simple pinches, called nodes, with finitely many symmetries once marked.
An algebra built from subspaces of a space, where multiplication records how they intersect.
The part of the Chow ring generated by the natural classes of the moduli space of curves.
A list of relations is complete when every true relation follows from it.
A coarser algebraic measurement of a space's shape; relations true in Chow stay true there.
A space that parametrizes quotients of a fixed sheaf, used here to produce an identity.
